entities.name: COVID-19 pandemic in Luxembourg
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary:
The COVID-19 pandemic in Luxembourg was a viral outbreak that took place in Luxembourg starting from 2020-02-29. It was a significant event in the region of Western Europe, affecting the lives of many people. The pandemic had a profound impact on the country's healthcare system and economy, leading to widespread lockdowns and restrictions.

The pandemic was caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, which was first identified in Wuhan, China in December 2019. The virus spread rapidly across the globe, infecting millions of people and causing a significant number of deaths. The pandemic was a major challenge for healthcare systems worldwide, leading to a global response to combat its spread.

The pandemic had a lasting impact on Luxembourg's society and economy. It led to a significant increase in remote work and online learning, changing the way people lived and worked. The pandemic also led to a renewed focus on public health and the importance of preparedness and response to global health crises.

One of the most striking statistics from the pandemic is the number of people who were vaccinated. According to official reports, over 80% of the Luxembourg population received a COVID-19 vaccine, making it one of the most vaccinated countries in the world.
